name: Spastic Paraplegia-Glaucoma-Intellectual Disability Syndrome
aliases: Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia with Glaucoma and Intellectual Disability

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Spastic Paraplegia-Glaucoma-Intellectual Disability Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Presence of early-onset glaucoma confirmed by ophthalmological examination
Mild to moderate intellectual disability documented by neuropsychological assessment
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Brain MRI showing corticospinal tract abnormalities or normal findings

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: progressive spastic paraplegia, early-onset glaucoma, and intellectual disability
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

imaging: Brain MRI may show corticospinal tract hyperintensities or be normal
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with hereditary spastic paraplegia (specific gene not yet fully characterized)
other: Ophthalmological examination confirming elevated intraocular pressure and optic nerve changes

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of glaucoma and intellectual disability
Diabetes mellitus and diabetes insipidus present

redFlags: Rapid progression of spasticity with loss of ambulation
references: Recent literature on hereditary spastic paraplegia with ocular involvement
